analysis.headline: Shares Your Data Broadly
analysis.quote: As a global organization, information about you can be shared globally throughout Oracle’s worldwide organization for a business purpose.

analysis.headline: Shares with Partners
analysis.quote: We may share personal information with the following third parties for a commercial purpose: Oracle partners such as internet security companies or retailers, for analytics on site security and site or internet performance.

analysis.headline: Extensive Device Performance Tracking
analysis.quote: Information related to your device’s performance when accessing and utilizing the internet, including time to resolve DNS, time spent making request, time spent downloading the response, and the total time between the response and the site loading (collectively referred to as “Internet Performance”).

analysis.headline: Retains Data for 12 Months
analysis.quote: Oracle maintains personal information collected by the Internet Performance Tools for up to 12 months as of the moment it was first collected by the Internet Performance Tools.

analysis.headline: Limited Access Rights
analysis.quote: Thus, requests to access, amend, correct, or delete data collected via the Internet Performance Tools would create a burden or expense disproportionate to the risks to your privacy.

analysis.headline: Collects Indirect Identifiers
analysis.quote: Personal information is information collected online by the Internet Performance Tools and may indirectly identify you, which includes: IP address and port Country, State, and City IP address of recursive DNS provider Time and date of query Domain queried Query details (e.g., TTL, query type, DNS flags, DNSSEC info) Query response

analysis.headline: Global Data Transfers
analysis.quote: If personal information is transferred to an Oracle recipient in a country that does not provide an adequate level of protection for personal information under applicable data protection law in the country where such information was collected, Oracle will take adequate measures designed to protect the personal information, such as ensuring that such transfers are subject to EU Model Clauses, Oracle’s BCR-P, or other adequate transfer mechanism as required under relevant data protection laws.
